title: Chapter 235: The Old Lady Outside the Elevator
html:
After entering the elevator, Chen Ge pressed the button for the twenty-third floor. The silver-gray doors slowly closed, sealing him away from the outside world. His breathing grew uneven. He disliked elevators—not because he was claustrophobic, but because he hated feeling trapped in an enclosed space.

The elevator’s number kept jumping.

Looks like Wang Xin’s mother was right; the tenants here rarely take the elevator at night.

The elevator climbed quickly, and the display soon reached 23. A chime sounded, and the doors opened. Light spilled into the corridor, only to be swallowed by the darkness. Closed doors lined both sides.

Reached the top so quickly?

The twenty-third floor looked much like every other level, except that a window at the corridor’s end stood open, allowing the wind to howl inside.

It does feel weird taking the elevator alone at night.

When the doors closed, Chen Ge pressed the button for the second floor. The elevator descended and soon arrived.

What is the point of this ritual? Will repeating it truly take me to the hidden twenty-fourth floor?

The doors closed, and Chen Ge traveled up to the twenty-second floor. Each time the elevator started or stopped, the change in speed produced a momentary shift in gravity—the reason some people grew lightheaded while riding one.

Chen Ge was physically fit, yet five minutes of continuous ascent and descent left him uncomfortable. His heart raced, and he could not calm it. It felt as though something were about to happen. After several repetitions, an inexplicable sense of foreboding settled over him.

The elevator descended from the eighteenth floor to the seventh, and he selected the seventeenth. Nothing had gone wrong so far, making the Ghost Stories Society’s instructions feel more like a psychological exercise than a supernatural ritual.

The elevator rose, the numbers changing steadily. It slowed, and the doors opened. Chen Ge leaned forward to look outside.

The corridor was empty. The tenants appeared to be asleep, and the building was silent.

I’ve been lucky not to encounter anyone. A few more trips should take me to the twenty-fourth floor.

Chen Ge had gotten used to the process. When he pressed the button, his eyes went to the number. The red number made his arm hang in mid-air.

16?

He was certain he had selected the seventeenth floor. Its button still glowed on the panel, yet the elevator had inexplicably stopped on the sixteenth.

Someone has called for the elevator on this floor!

Chen Ge bent slightly, lowering his right hand toward the cleaver strapped to his calf. He surveyed the empty elevator, fully alert. The corridor outside was pitch-black; he could see no more than ten meters into it. Everything was silent.

Could it be a prank?

That idea was immediately rejected by Chen Ge.

Several seconds later, the doors slowly closed. Chen Ge stared around the empty car without lowering his guard. Something invisible might now be standing beside him. He slipped a hand into his left pocket and checked his phone: 12:01 a.m. Wednesday had begun.

The elevator continued upward and stopped at the seventeenth floor. Chen Ge leaned against the wall and selected the eighth, but before long, something else happened.

The elevator stopped on the 11th floor, and after the door opened, Chen Ge saw a white dress hanging in the middle of the corridor.

Something else is getting on the elevator?

There was no wind, yet the dress swayed as though advancing toward the elevator. Chen Ge lunged for the close-door button. The garment began whipping more violently, like someone sprinting down the corridor.

Close the f*cking door!

The doors closed when the dress was only two or three meters away, and the elevator resumed its descent. Chen Ge sagged into a corner, his palms slick with cold sweat. From that moment onward, the building felt different. The elevator reached the eighth floor without incident, and he remained there for a moment.

According to the flyer, he had to travel to the sixteenth floor next, which meant passing the level with the white dress. He feared the elevator might stop and open on the eleventh, where the dress would be waiting.

His finger stopped at the control panel for a long time as he tried to convince himself.

I have the Pen Spirit and Xu Yin with me. If the thing dares to do anything, I have the advantage in numbers.

The elevator rose. When the display reached 11, Chen Ge’s heart skipped, but the car did not stop. The number continued upward. Before he could relax, however, the elevator halted on the thirteenth floor.

Someone else is coming in?

The doors slowly opened. An elderly woman in dark clothing and a thick scarf stood outside. Deep wrinkles folded across her face, her hair was entirely silver, and layers of heavy fabric concealed her limbs.

She had not expected anyone to be inside, and surprise crossed her face.

“Strange...” she murmured. The doors closed while she remained where she was. “Why are so many people riding the elevator this late? There isn’t even room for me.”

When Chen Ge heard the old lady, cold sweat broke out on his forehead. It looked like he really did not have the advantage in numbers. No wonder the Pen Spirit has been acting so calmly. She didn’t even warn me.

He looked around, but he could only see himself inside the elevator. Thinking back to what the old lady said, Chen Ge’s heart raced even faster.

Something is wrong. Even inside the Third Sick Hall, I wasn’t this nervous.Chen Ge tried to steady himself, but an instinctive warning lodged in his mind: he was in grave danger.

That old lady is suspicious as well. Wearing all black and a scarf so late at night, is she that cold?

After the encounter with the old woman, the rest of the ritual proceeded without incident. Just as she had said, the elevator was already full; no one outside could enter even if they wished to.
